may already be occurring. Persons along rivers and streams in the
warned area should take immediate precautions to protect life and
property.

forecast precipitation 24 hours into the future. Changes to the
rainfall forecast, or any additional rainfall after 24 hours, may
cause changes to these river forecasts.

properties.headline: Flood Warning issued September 22 at 9:00PM EDT by NWS Tampa Bay Ruskin FL
properties.description:
...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in Florida...

Withlacoochee At US 41 Dunnellon affecting Marion, Citrus and Levy
Counties.

.The Withlacoochee River at Dunnellon has been steadily rising since
July, and on September 15 reached flood stage. The cause of the high
water along the Withlacoochee River at Dunnellon is due to excessive
hydrilla growth (from the river bottom to the water surface) along a
4.5 mile stretch of river between US 41 and Lake Rousseau.  The
hydrilla is acting like a dam and holding water back, causing water
levels to rise.

* WHAT...Minor flooding is occurring and is forecast to continue.

* WHERE...Withlacoochee at US 41 Dunnellon.

* WHEN...Until further notice.

* IMPACTS...At 28.2 feet, Docks and boat ramps flood along the river
in Citrus and Marion counties.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 8:45 PM EDT Tuesday the stage was 28.2 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 28.2 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to hold steady at flood stage.
Additional rises are possible.
- Flood stage is 28.2 feet.
- Flood History...This crest compares to a previous crest of 28.2
feet on 10/02/1979.
- https://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

properties.headline: Flash Flood Warning issued September 23 at 2:39AM EDT until September 23 at 5:45AM EDT by NWS Greenville-Spartanburg SC
properties.description:
At 239 AM EDT, Doppler radar indicated thunderstorms producing heavy
rain across the warned area. Between 2.5 and 4 inches of rain have
fallen. Flash flooding is ongoing or expected to begin shortly.

HAZARD...Life threatening flash flooding. Thunderstorms producing
flash flooding.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Life threatening flash flooding of creeks and streams, urban
areas, highways, streets and underpasses.

Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
Lake Lure, Chimney Rock Village, Chimney Rock State Park, Bat Cave
and Gerton.

Rutherford County Emergency Management has activated their flash
flood warning sirens for the Falls Creek area just north of Chimney
Rock. Residents and visitors impacted are strongly encouraged to move
away from the river and seek higher ground immediately. If you are
staying near the Rocky Broad River in the Chimney Rock/Lake Lure area
please maintain situational awareness and closely monitor weather
conditions and water levels. Conditions can change rapidly and water
levels may rise with little warning. Please continue to monitor
trusted weather sources, local emergency notifications, and official
Rutherford County Emergency Management updates for addition
information.

Rutherford County Emergency Management reported water over the
roadway at times on Main Street in Chimney Rock as well as flood
waters beginning to cross the temporary road north of Chimney Rock in
the Falls Creek area.

Flood stage has dropped to 6.78 feet at the Rocky Broad River near
Bat Cave. Some campgrounds below Bat Cave in Rutherford County near
Lake Lure may be evacuated as a precaution.
properties.instruction:
Be especially cautious at night when it is harder to recognize the
dangers of flooding.

Be aware of your surroundings and do not drive on flooded roads.

properties.headline: Flash Flood Warning issued September 22 at 11:46PM MDT until September 23 at 1:45AM MDT by NWS El Paso Tx/Santa Teresa NM
properties.description:
At 1146 PM MDT, Thunderstorms have diminished in intensity over the
Otero Mesa. Radar estimates 2.50 to 3 inches of rain fell in Otero
County, northwest of Dell City. This will result in flooding in
various draws that flow towards Dell City. Retention dams will
prevent water from reaching Dell City, but flooding will impact rural
roads north and northwest of town, especially across the New Mexico
border.

HAZARD...Flash flooding caused by thunderstorms.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Flash flooding of small creeks and streams, urban areas,
highways, streets and underpasses as well as other poor
drainage and low-lying areas.

Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
Rural areas on the Otero Mesa northwest of Dell City.
properties.instruction:
Be especially cautious at night when it is harder to recognize the
dangers of flooding.

Be aware of your surroundings and do not drive on flooded roads.

Remain alert for flooding even in locations not receiving rain.
Arroyos, streams, and rivers can become raging killer currents in a
matter of minutes, even from distant rainfall.
